simple: Every Roblox game comes with built-in screens like the player list, health bar, backpack, chat, and emotes menu. Sometimes you want to hide them, for example during a cutscene or because you made your own versions. This page lists those built-in parts and shows how to turn them off from a client script.
analogy: It is like a TV that shows the channel logo and volume bar on screen. You can turn those off when you want a clean picture.
keyPoints: Hide built-in UI with `StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled()` and an `Enum.CoreGuiType` value, set to `false`.
`PlayerList` is the leaderboard, `Health` is the health bar, `Backpack` is the tool hotbar, and `Chat` is the text chat window.
`EmotesMenu`, `SelfView`, `Captures`, and `AvatarSwitcher` are other built-in pieces you can hide.
The health bar only shows when the character is hurt, and the backpack only shows when it has tools.
Run this from a client script, such as a LocalScript, because UI lives on each player's screen.
On touch devices, hide the on-screen thumbstick and jump button with `GuiService.TouchControlsEnabled = false`.

terms.CoreGui: The built-in Roblox screens that every game has, like chat and the player list.
terms.CoreGuiType: An enum that names each built-in screen, like `Enum.CoreGuiType.Health`.
terms.client script: A script that runs on the player's device, like a LocalScript.
terms.thumbstick: The on-screen circle that phone and tablet players drag to move.
terms.Self View: A small window showing a player's own avatar face. It only shows if the player turned it on.

example.title: Hide the health bar and backpack
example.code:
local StarterGui = game:GetService("StarterGui")

-- Turn off the built-in health bar and tool hotbar
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Health, false)
StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, false)

-- Later, you can turn one back on with true
-- StarterGui:SetCoreGuiEnabled(Enum.CoreGuiType.Backpack, true)
explain: Each `SetCoreGuiEnabled` call picks one built-in screen and sets it to `false` to hide it.
Passing `true` instead shows it again, which is handy after a cutscene ends.

watchOut: Calling `SetCoreGuiEnabled` from a server Script. It has to run on the client.
Hiding the backpack while players still need their tools. Give them another way to equip tools, or they will be stuck.
